newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Black consortium wins Zimbabwe cell phone tender.
newsitem.headline: Black consortium wins Zimbabwe cell phone tender.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government awarded a consortium of black businessmen on Thursday night a licence to operate the country's first private cellular telephone network, despite a presidential directive to licence a private firm that has been battling for approval for the past three years.

Telecommunications Minister Joyce Mujuru said Telecel, a consortium of black businesses and a firm based in Zaire, had won the licence, whose award was delayed by court challenges mounted by private company Econet.

Mujuru said in a statement her ministry had instructed Telecel to award shares ranging between 15 and 20 percent to four companies, including Econet, who were also bidding to provide the country's first private cellular telephone network.
On the presidential instructions, she said Mugabe had directed her to see the tender through and award the licence according to the law.

However, the official Herald newspaper reported on Friday that Vice President Joshua Nkomo said Econet, owned by local black businessman Strive Masiyiwa, should be licensed in its own right as per President Robert Mugabe's instructions this week.

"We don't do things like that in this country. The young man (Masiyiwa) was running around and now they are taking things from him. That is not acceptable. We will sit down and discuss this matter," Nkomo is quoted as saying.

He said if there were any problems about the presidential instructions, Mujuru and the government tender board should have referred back to him or waited for Mugabe to come back from his European trip.

Masiyiwa, who has been engaged in court battles for the past three years to get a licence to operate a cellular telephone service, told reporters there was an arrangement for him to operate a third network.
The first licence was awarded to the state-owned Posts and Telecommunications Corporation last year.
Last week Masiyiwa withdrew his latest court challenge on the issue on the understanding he would be awarded a licence.
